fx_rate_note: 1 NZD = 0.5869 USD as of 2026-08-04 (live). Historical multiples also use this flat rate as an approximation (task-directed simplification); true historical FX ranged ~0.57-0.62 across FY-end dates, so historical EV/EBITDA multiples below carry minor imprecision from this approximation.

inputs.net_debt_note: FY2026 (Mar-2026): TotalDebt 27.3 - Cash 2.2 = 25.1. Task prompt cited 25.2 informally; 25.1 is the CSV-precise figure and is used throughout.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: ArborGen holds NET DEBT (net debt $25.1m), not net cash, so there is no double-count risk from interest income. Interest received FY2026 was only $0.5m (immaterial) and is left inside reported FCF; cash INTEREST PAID ($2.5m) is separately modeled as a real cost of debt in the owner-FCF component build below.
inputs.sbc_source: 10-K equivalent: ArborGen FY2026 Annual Report, Statement of Changes in Equity (movement in share-based payment reserve, $0.4m) cross-checked against Metrics.csv StockBasedComp column ($0.6m FY2026, $0.0m FY2025, $1.3m FY2024). SBC is negligible and non-dilutive at this company's scale; treated as immaterial per task guidance (~$0.5-0.6m/yr).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2026 buyback/warrant repurchase cash outflow = $0.0m (FY2025 was $0.5m). No material, ongoing buyback program; SBC is small enough that uncovered dilution is treated as negligible.
inputs.last_fcf_note: Owner FCF FY2026 = reported FCF (-0.4) - SBC (0.6) - interest income (0.0) = -1.0. This is the SBC-adjusted actual; the forward projection is NOT extrapolated from this single noisy year but rebuilt from Adjusted EBITDA/D&A/interest/tax/capex/working-capital components per Step 1c, because FY2026 reported FCF/EBITDA conversion is not representative of a steady state (see fcf_base_year_documentation).

fcf_base_year_documentation.why_not_flat_extrapolation: FY2026 reported FCF was -$0.4m and Adjusted EBITDA was $11.5m - a near-zero cash conversion year. Historical FCF FY2019-26 (USD m): -3.3, -4.6, +5.2, +2.9, +0.9, +5.1, -5.1, -0.4; median is only ~+0.2m. ArborGen has NEVER produced sustained positive FCF at scale - capex ($4-9m/yr), interest on ~$27m of debt (~$2.5m/yr cash interest paid), and working-capital swings (inventory/seed WIP builds with growth, seasonal H2-weighted receivables) consume nearly all EBITDA most years. Extrapolating Adjusted EBITDA growth into FCF the company has never delivered would materially overstate value.
fcf_base_year_documentation.component_build_used: Adjusted EBITDA (revenue x ebitda_margin path, ramping FY2026's 16.9% toward a modest maturity level) minus SBC (% of revenue, ~0.9% declining to 0.6%) minus D&A (% of revenue, driven heavily by $54.1m intellectual property amortised over 17 years, a large NON-CASH charge that is added back after the EBIT/tax step) minus cash interest (declining % of revenue as Ridgeville building-sale proceeds are earmarked for debt paydown) minus cash tax (ramped from FY2026's low observed ~10% effective cash-tax burden, reflecting Brazil-only cash taxpaying status while US NOLs shelter US income, toward the 28% NZ/US-blended statutory rate used in the FY2026 tax reconciliation note) minus capex (held near the $6.3-7.6m FY2019-26 average dollar level, NOT scaled up as a flat % of a growing revenue base, per task guidance) plus/minus working capital (modelled as -18% of the YoY revenue INCREASE, i.e. a cash use when growing, consistent with FY2026's actual $6.0m working-capital cash drag against $5.0m of revenue growth).
fcf_base_year_documentation.terminal_year_fcf_margin_still_immature: Base-case owner-FCF margin rises from 3.0% (Y1) to only 5.9% (Y10) and is STILL RISING at Y10 - it never reaches a flat steady state within the 10-year horizon because D&A (dominated by the fixed-dollar IP amortisation charge) declines only slowly as a % of a compounding revenue base. This is the trigger for the terminal-value sanity-bound fix documented in sanity_check below: a pure Gordon-growth capitalisation of this still-immature, thin FCF margin produces an implied exit multiple far below any multiple the market has paid for ArborGen in 10 years, so the terminal value is bound to a defensible EV/Adjusted-EBITDA range instead.

historical_growth.eps_note: EPS/earnings CAGR not meaningful - net income positive in only 2 of the last 8 fiscal years (FY2021 $3.2m, FY2022 $1.7m); all other years show losses (FY2025 -$21.5m includes a $21.8m non-cash IP impairment).
historical_growth.fcf_cagr_note: FCF CAGR not computable/meaningful - the FY2019-26 owner-FCF series alternates sign nearly every year (-3.3, -4.6, +5.2, +2.9, +0.9, +3.8, -5.1, -1.0 USD m) with no consistent trend; median owner FCF across the period is roughly break-even.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity (book value) CAGR is NEGATIVE (-4.3% to -7.3%) while revenue CAGR is POSITIVE (+4.8% to +6.7%) - a divergence far in excess of the 30% threshold. This is NOT a sign of value destruction in the operating business; it is driven almost entirely by two non-cash intangible impairments ($21.8m FY2025, $1.7m FY2026) against the $54.1m carrying value of acquired forestry-genetics IP. Equity/book-value CAGR is therefore REJECTED as the growth driver for this company and revenue CAGR (7-year, through-cycle, matching the task's guidance of ~4.8%/yr) is used instead, consistent with the qualitative view that Brazil growth and US structural decline roughly net to a low-single-digit blended rate.

build_up.micro_cap_illiquidity_premium_pct: +2.0 to +2.5 (market cap ~US$16-19m, well under the $300m liquidity threshold; thin NZX trading volumes)
build_up.earnings_cyclicality_weather_crop_premiu: +1.5 (uninsured outdoor crops; weather materially affected saleable volume in both US and Brazil in FY26)
build_up.structural_decline_uncertainty_premium_p: +1.0 to +2.0 (management explicitly frames US South pulp/paper decline as structural, not cyclical, in the company's LARGEST single segment)
build_up.base_case_selection: 16.0% (mid-range); bull 14.5% (assumes leadership stabilises, Brazil execution de-risks, debt reduced via Ridgeville sale); bear 18.0% (leadership vacuum + rising net debt + structural decline all compound)

horizon_rationale: Base and bull owner-FCF margins are STILL RISING at Year 10 (base: 3.0% -> 5.9%; bull: 3.3% -> 8.6%), so a 5-year horizon would capitalise an immature margin in perpetuity and understate value; a 10-year explicit build was used per Step 1c(d). Even at Year 10 the margin has not fully matured, which is the direct cause of the terminal-value sanity-bound fix below.

entry_price.methodology: Entry price = price at which buying today, collecting 10 years of BASE-CASE projected owner FCF, and exiting at the year-10 fair value earns a 15% IRR. Terminal value uses the SAME sanity-bound (floor/cap EV/Adjusted-EBITDA) methodology as the intrinsic-value calculation, discounted back to today at the 15% hurdle rather than WACC (the hurdle is the buyer's required return; WACC/multiple bounds determine the FAIR exit price the buyer receives in year 10).

sensitivity.matrix_note: Columns (terminal growth) are flat within each WACC row because the base-case Gordon terminal value is below the EV/Adjusted-EBITDA floor bound (4.64x, the 10-year historical minimum multiple) across this entire WACC/growth range - the terminal value is floor-bound, not Gordon-bound, so terminal growth has no marginal effect on the dollar terminal value at these settings (only WACC affects the outcome, via the discount factor). This is itself a finding: the base-case DCF is EV/EBITDA-multiple-driven, not growth-driven, at every plausible WACC/terminal-growth combination tested.

probability_weighted.weighting_rationale: Bear weighted MOST heavily (45%, above the task's suggested midpoint) given: (1) management's own characterisation of the US South decline as STRUCTURAL rather than cyclical - the base case for the largest single segment; (2) net debt has risen for two consecutive years against a thin $2.2m cash balance, with no committed refinancing beyond the uncertain-timing Ridgeville building sale; (3) CEO resignation in June 2026 leaves only an interim CEO in place during a critical turnaround/Brazil-integration period; (4) two consecutive years of guidance cuts/impairments reduce confidence in management's own base-case numbers. Bull is weighted lowest (20%) because it requires BOTH a Brazil growth acceleration AND a benign US stabilisation to occur simultaneously with no further weather/crop shocks - a low-probability combination given the last two fiscal years' track record.

memo_sbc_noncash_value.note: SBC is immaterial at ArborGen (~$0.6m/yr, 0.9% of revenue) versus a company like DUOL where it is the dominant valuation lever. Treating SBC as fully non-cash (i.e. not deducting it from owner FCF at all) would add back only ~$0.6-1.0m/yr across the projection, which shifts base-case intrinsic value by roughly USD 0.0002-0.0004/share (NZD ~0.0003-0.0007/share) - immaterial to two decimal places on a stock priced at NZ$0.065. The SBC adjustment is applied for methodological consistency but is NOT a meaningful driver of this valuation, unlike the terminal-value/multiple-bound issue documented in sanity_check.

historical_multiples.fx_note: Flat NZDUSD=0.5869 approximation applied to all FY-end market caps for consistency (true historical FX varied ~0.57-0.62); minor imprecision acknowledged.
historical_multiples.p_e_note: Positive earnings in only 2 of 8 FY-end points (FY2021 15.1x, FY2022 41.7x) - too thin a sample for a reliable P/E anchor; P/B and EV/Adjusted-EBITDA are the primary multiples used in the sanity check. Historical P/E, where it exists, would use SBC-adjusted (i.e. as-reported, since SBC is immaterial here) earnings and will not exactly match a screener's P/E in years where SBC was disclosed (FY2024+).

trip_rules_evaluated.result: NOT tripped in the high direction. Base-case implied P/B = 0.092x on FY2026 book value, vs 10yr max 0.47x.
NOT tripped in the high direction. Base-case implied EV/Adj.EBITDA (on FY2026 ACTUAL EBITDA of $11.5m) = 3.13x, vs 10yr max 11.30x.

trip_rules_evaluated.result: NOT tripped: base-case upside is -43.3% (a DOWNSIDE), not >100%, and price (NZ$0.065) is at the 10-year LOW, i.e. the bottom of the range, not the upper half. Correctly does not trip per the literal rule.

additional_check_performed.description: The four standard trip rules are all written to catch DCF OVERvaluation (IV implausibly high vs history). This ticker's initial (pre-fix) DCF build produced the MIRROR-IMAGE failure - an implausibly LOW valuation, below any multiple the market has EVER paid for ArborGen in 10 years, even at the stock's lowest-ever multiple. An additional symmetric check was therefore applied and IS reported here even though it falls outside the four literal rules.
additional_check_performed.trip_reason: Pre-fix base-case intrinsic value (NZ$0.005/share) implied a P/B of 0.013x - roughly 1/19th of the stock's 10-year historical MINIMUM P/B (0.24x) - and an EV/Adjusted-EBITDA of 2.3x on FY2026's actual $11.5m Adjusted EBITDA, versus a 10-year historical MINIMUM of 4.64x. The market has never, even during the FY2025 impairment-driven trough, capitalised this business below either floor. A DCF landing materially below the worst multiple the market has ever assigned signals a modelling problem, not a genuine mispricing opportunity.

sanity_check.diagnosis: The component-built owner FCF is genuine and correctly excludes one-off items, but the business is structurally low-FCF-conversion: D&A is dominated by a large, largely fixed-dollar, NON-CASH intellectual-property amortisation charge ($54.1m carrying value / 17 years). Owner-FCF margin is still climbing at Year 10 (base: 3.0% -> 5.9%) and never reaches a mature steady state within the explicit horizon. Applying pure Gordon-growth capitalisation (FCF_10 x (1+g) / (WACC-g)) to this still-thin, still-rising terminal FCF produces a terminal value equivalent to only 2.3-3.3x EV/EBITDA across scenarios - far below the multiple range (4.64x-11.30x) the market has actually paid for ArborGen across every point in the last 10 fiscal years, including the FY2025/26 impairment-driven trough. This is a variant of the 'terminal margin still immature -> Gordon undervalues' trap described in the DCF methodology's Step 1c(d)/Step 4 guidance, except here it manifests as an UNDER-valuation relative to history rather than the more commonly-flagged OVER-valuation case. The existing 'terminal value = lower of Gordon or Cap' rule protects only against Gordon being too HIGH; it does not protect against Gordon being pathologically LOW relative to any multiple ever realised.
sanity_check.fix_applied: Bound the terminal value within a defensible EV/Adjusted-EBITDA multiple RANGE anchored to the ticker's own 10-year historical trading multiples, rather than using Gordon growth uncapped on the low side: Base scenario floor=10yr historical MINIMUM (4.64x), cap=10yr historical AVERAGE (7.35x); Bull scenario floor=10yr AVERAGE (7.35x), cap=10yr MAXIMUM (11.30x); Bear scenario floor=60% of the 10yr minimum (2.78x, reflecting a further de-rating consistent with the bear narrative), cap=10yr MINIMUM (4.64x). Gordon growth is used only when it falls inside the scenario's floor/cap band; in practice Gordon fell BELOW the floor in all three scenarios at the assumed WACC/terminal-growth settings, so all three scenarios are floor-bound (terminal value = floor multiple x terminal-year Adjusted EBITDA).

bear.note: Bear-case equity value is NEGATIVE (-USD 18.1m / NZ$-0.061 per share). This is NOT floored to zero - it is retained as an honest signal that the bear scenario (structural US decline continuing, weather shocks, no debt paydown) implies enterprise value insufficient to cover net debt, i.e. a real risk of equity impairment/recapitalisation, consistent with the risk factors in the qualitative analysis (rising net debt, thin cash, uninsured crops).

sanity_check.post_fix_result: Base-case IV NZ$0.037/share (-43.3% vs current NZ$0.065), Bull NZ$0.182/share (+180.1%, close to Forsyth Barr's independent NZ$0.20 DCF), Bear NZ$-0.061/share (equity impairment risk). All three now sit within or reference the historical multiple range rather than implying a valuation below any multiple the market has ever assigned.
sanity_check.note_pb_pe_screener_mismatch: Historical P/E figures above use SBC-adjusted (here, effectively as-reported, since SBC is immaterial at ArborGen) earnings and are computed only for the 2 of 8 fiscal years with positive net income; these will not match a stock screener's trailing P/E for loss-making years (screener P/E is typically blank/n.m. for a loss).
sanity_check.passed_note: Initial (pre-fix) build FAILED an ADDITIONAL symmetric check (implied multiples below any 10-year historical minimum) beyond the four literal trip rules, none of which technically tripped on their own terms. After applying the floor/cap terminal-value fix, the model PASSES: all three scenarios' implied exit multiples now sit at or within the ticker's own 10-year historical EV/Adjusted-EBITDA range.

valuation_philosophy.summary: ArborGen is a capital-intensive, D&A-heavy, currently loss-making forestry-genetics company whose largest segment (US South, ~56% of revenue) management itself describes as in STRUCTURAL decline. Owner FCF, built bottom-up from Adjusted EBITDA less real cash costs (SBC, interest, cash tax, maintenance capex, working capital), is thin and has never been reliably positive at scale (median FY2019-26 owner FCF is roughly break-even). A pure income-approach (Gordon growth) DCF on this FCF, however methodologically correct, capitalises a terminal margin that is still immature at Year 10 and produces terminal values below any multiple of Adjusted EBITDA the market has paid for this stock across a full 10-year cycle including its worst impairment-driven trough. The valuation therefore blends the income approach (explicit 10-year owner-FCF build, discounted at a WACC that reflects micro-cap illiquidity, earnings cyclicality and structural-decline uncertainty) with a market-based sanity bound (the stock's own historical EV/Adjusted-EBITDA trading range) for the terminal value, consistent with the DCF framework's existing 'lower of Gordon or Cap' discipline extended symmetrically to a floor.
valuation_philosophy.why_iv_still_below_market_price_in_base_: Even after the terminal-value fix, base-case IV (NZ$0.037) sits below the already-10-year-low market price (NZ$0.065). This reflects: (1) the WACC build-up (16% base, itemised for illiquidity/cyclicality/structural-decline premiums) being meaningfully higher than a standard small-cap discount rate; (2) revenue growth capped at the through-cycle 4.8%/yr historical CAGR rather than extrapolating Brazil's recent record growth; (3) a floor multiple (4.64x) anchored to the stock's OWN 10-year minimum multiple, which itself already embeds a meaningful discount for the risks now crystallising (leadership vacancy, rising net debt, US structural decline). The market price may be pricing in either (a) a probability-weighted outcome closer to the bull/base blend than this model's bear-heavy 45% weighting, or (b) takeout/asset-value optionality (Ridgeville building sale, IP carrying value) not explicitly modelled here. The probability-weighted IV (NZ$0.022) is materially below market, consistent with a bear-tilted read of a company in genuine transition with a thin balance-sheet buffer.
valuation_philosophy.confidence: LOW-MODERATE. This is a micro-cap, loss-making, currency-layered (USD-functional/NZD-quoted/BRL-exposed), leadership-in-transition company with a structurally declining core segment - wide, honest dispersion between scenarios (bear NZ$-0.06 to bull NZ$0.18) is the correct representation of genuine uncertainty, not a modelling defect.
